evidence_inputs: Section 8's own done_when asks for zero private-name imports between top-level modules; this node deliberately reaches 24 live sites behind an explicit exemption list, so section 8 cannot be collapsed on this head and owes at least one continuation node for the 24 entries. The rule keys exemptions on (module, name) and fails on a stale entry, so the list can only shrink. Independent census at 611ba81d3 reproduces the fragment's census exactly: 24 names across 18 statements, matching the exemption set one-for-one.

findings.fold_into: sn-pipeline-hygiene section 8 continuation closing the remaining 24 exemptions
findings.text: release_notes.py:34 (_run_git) and :41 (_github_slug) are a near-verbatim copy of catalog_release.py:401 and :1502, so the package now holds two github-slug parsers that will drift; the plan's done-when allows closure 'either by moving the caller or through a public name the owning module exports', and a copy is neither, while the parallel-agent ruling says a peer-touched file never blocks an edit. The remaining exemption promote.py:1994 _github_slug forces a later node to give catalog_release.py a public spelling, which is where this copy should be deleted; fold into the section's remaining-exemption node.

findings.text: The manifest's tests: line names test_package_import_boundaries.py::test_no_private_name_imports_between_top_level_modules plus the 13 sibling files, but the recorded head arm ran the whole test_package_import_boundaries.py file (test_logs header: 'pytest ... tests/standard_names/test_package_import_boundaries.py ...'), so the receipt promotion reads names a command neither arm actually ran; both pass, so this is a receipt-accuracy defect, not a gate result.
